messages:
sara: Heads-up — perf regression on Mistral7B dedicated pool after the kernel-picker change. Throughput down ~28% at seq=1024, tail latency up. Anyone else seeing this?

Tom: saw the same on canary. Tracing shows extra memcpy on the KV path when num_key_value_heads != model_heads and we hit the fallback kernel.

liam: Posting quick profile snippet (from canary run):
```
# top hot functions
memcpy: 48.3%
kv_slot_compact: 22.1%
kernel_fallback_dispatch: 15.4%
attention_kernel_v2: 8.7%
```

anita: Is this happening for both MQA and GQA configs or just MQA?

sara: Primarily MQA. Config used: num_key_value_heads=8 kv_dim=64 (MQA). GQA runs with num_key_value_heads=1 showed much smaller delta.

perf-bot: Regression alert R-2026-381 created (severity=medium). See https://perf.redwood/results/R-2026-381 :eyes:

tom: Root cause hypothesis: kernel-picker now prefers v2 kernels for memory layout X, but for MQA the stride doesn't align to warp and we fall back to a generic path that does a lot more slot compaction + memcpy.

liam: Also seeing paged-KV fragmentation on long-lived sessions with paging enabled. Compaction frequency spikes after ~20k tokens which exacerbates CPU/mem churn.

anita: Quick mitigation options: 1) revert kernel-picker change, 2) add a targeted kernel-policy (force classic for Mistral MQA when (kv_heads*kv_dim)%64 != 0), 3) increase slab size to reduce fragmentation.

sara: I tried slab tweaks: slab=128MB -> worse, slab=256MB -> returns to baseline throughput but we saw OOMs on smaller instance types in dedicated pool. Not safe as a global change.

tom: Suggestion: implement a batching heuristic change instead of global slab increase. Cap batches by effective_kv_bytes rather than tokens. Example heuristic:
```
effective_kv_bytes = batch_size * (kv_heads * kv_dim * 8)
if effective_kv_bytes > KV_BYTES_CAP: split batch
```
This prevents huge compactions in mixed-heads workloads.

liam: I pushed a small kernel hint patch to feature/kv-hint which pins the old kernel for Mistral MQA when alignment mismatch detected. CI perf run queued.

perf-bot: Perf job finished for canary: throughput -18% vs baseline (not as bad as dedicated), tail +45ms. Details: https://perf.redwood/results/R-2026-381

anita: We should also add a paged-KV compaction throttle: e.g., max_compactions_per_sec=2 per-device and backoff on memory pressure. That would reduce jitter during long sessions.

tom: Plan proposed: 1) rollback kernel-picker on dedicated canaries immediately, 2) land kv-hint patch, 3) add batching cap by effective_kv_bytes, 4) add paged-KV compaction throttle and run a 48h stress.

sara: I'll open the rollout doc and schedule the rollback for the dedicated pool. Tagging @oncall for immediate visibility. :rotating_light:

oncall: Acknowledged — I'll standby and monitor post-rollback.

liam: For follow-up, we should add a perf test matrix: Mistral/Mixtral with MQA heads {4,8,16} x kv_dim {32,64,128} x seq {512,1024,2048} and measure fallback-frequency + memcpy ratio.

sara: Agreed. Also add a kernel-picker unit that simulates warp alignment to avoid surprises.

tom: One more note — Qwen paths get ~6% gain from v2 kernel, so we need a targeted policy rather than full revert. We'll gate by model+config.

anita: I'll draft the policy table after we have the perf matrix.

sara: Thanks everyone. Opening the rollback PR now and will report back with canary numbers. :thumbsup:
